name: MAX7219 LED Display Driver
summary: Drives eight 7-segment digits or an 8x8 matrix over three wires, with its own BCD decoder, brightness control and scanning. No refresh code at all.
notes: Both GND pins, 4 and 9, must be connected. Wiring only one works on the bench and then flickers.
ISET takes a resistor to V+, not to ground. That resistor sets peak segment current: around 10k for 40 mA, 28k for about 20 mA. Leaving it open means no light; shorting it destroys the chip.
It scans the digits itself at about 800 Hz and holds the data, so you write once and walk away. There is no refresh loop to run.

The digit and segment pins are scattered around the package in no sensible order. A matrix wired by eye instead of by pin number comes out transposed or mirrored, which is the single most common MAX7219 complaint.
Brightness is both digital, 16 steps over SPI, and analog through ISET. Set the coarse level with the resistor and trim in software.
Decode mode turns raw segment control into BCD digits per position. Turn it off for a matrix or for custom glyphs, on for numeric displays.
The MAX7221 is the same part with SPI-compliant timing and slew-limited segment drivers for less RFI. It also respects CS properly, which matters on a shared bus.
Peak current across all eight digits can reach 330 mA. The cheap modules do not decouple well; add 100 uF if the display dims as digits light.

pins.name: DIN
pins.note: This is MOSI. Sampled on the rising edge of CLK.

pins.name: DIG0
pins.note: Digit drivers are scattered across the package in no useful order. Wire from the numbers.

pins.name: GND
pins.note: Both ground pins, 4 and 9, must be connected. One is not enough.

pins.name: LOAD
pins.note: Rising edge latches the last 16 bits. This is CS.

pins.name: SEG F
pins.note: Segment order on the package is scrambled too: A, F, B, G down this side.

pins.name: ISET
pins.note: A resistor from here to V+ sets segment current. 10k gives roughly 40 mA per segment; never leave it open or short it.

pins.name: V+
pins.note: 5 V. Needs 10 uF and 100 nF right at the pin; eight digits strobing is a hard load.

pins.name: DOUT
pins.note: Feed into the next chip's DIN to chain displays. Data appears 16.5 clocks later.

circuit.title: Minimum circuit

parts.why: RSET sets the peak segment current, about 100 times the ISET current. Table 11 of the datasheet gives 11.8 kOhm for 40 mA into a 2 V LED.
The datasheet asks for this next to the part. Scanning digits pull current in hard bursts.
The ceramic half of the same job, as close to the pin as it will go.

circuit.note: Both GND pins, 4 and 9, must be connected. 40 mA per segment is the recommended maximum; above that you need external digit drivers.
